summary: Job-scoped chat integration (iter 62) fully validated end-to-end. 10/10 backend integration tests pass. All 8 UI flows from the review request pass: MyJobsTab Message button navigates to /chat/{job_id}?with={applicant_uid}; ChatHeader renders the gold Briefcase job bar with title/area/'Open to offers'/JOB pill; message send + reload persistence works both sides; applicant inbox at /dashboard?tab=messages shows 'Job: <title>' label (with is_job_thread:true); applicant can click into the same job-bar thread; regression: property chat still renders Building2 property bar (no job bar); edge case: /chat/<fake_uuid> renders empty chat page gracefully with no crash and no job bar; cleanup DELETE succeeds.
critical_code_review_comments: chat.py get_conversations correctly uses `_id` (UUID) on the marketplace_jobs fallback — matches jobs.py's storage schema. Good.
Chat.js fetchProperty falls back to /marketplace/jobs/{id} only on ANY error (not strictly 404). Slightly loose — but Axios throws for all non-2xx so behavior is equivalent in practice.
ChatHeader gates the job bar with `!property && job`, so if BOTH resolve (never happens today) the property bar wins. Sensible priority.
Job info bar has 'Open to offers' as a hardcoded English string (not i18n'd), while the property bar uses translated `rental_type` labels. Minor i18n inconsistency for future polish — not blocking.

MyJobsTab passes `app.provider?.user_id` to the chat URL. If enrichment ever returns null (e.g. deleted provider row), the URL becomes `?with=undefined`. Consider disabling the Message button when user_id is missing.

Job chat threads store messages with `property_id=<job_uuid>` — that overloading is documented in chat.py comments but the field name in db.messages is now semantically 'thread_id'. Consider a schema note in models.py.
